method.workload: Frozen nine-stone stack, 49 inventory stones, seed 0, 1024 iterations, evaluation batch 256, four CPU result workers, 240-second limit with 30-second reserve.
method.timing: Sequential isolated processes; search-only wall time excludes setup/teardown; OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1.
method.ordering: Three candidates followed by a fresh 32/128 control. Prior control retained from the preceding iteration experiment.
method.scope: Process-local batch overrides only; production defaults unchanged.
method.limitations: Single seed and scene; one run per candidate. Small differences require repetition. Native call counts cover simulation only. Stage timers include native host/result work; overlap is with CUDA wrapper intervals, not measured GPU-kernel execution.

conclusion: 128/512 minimizes calls and is fastest in this single-seed screening: 36 calls, 168.945 seconds, 6.298 evaluated nodes/s, 1.113 expanded parents/s. 64/256 is only 1.110 seconds slower. Differences are modest; no production defaults changed.
validation: All runs complete 1024 iterations, evaluate 1064 candidates, expand 188 distinct parents, leave no pending nodes, and match the previous ordered-tree, native module, and Python source hashes.
